the interactions of the vascular endothelial cell growth factors, VEGF-A, VEGF-C and VEGF-D, and their cognate receptor tyrosine kinase receptors, Flt-1, KDR and Flt-4.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Flt-1, like VEGFR2, can interact with PLC gamma and that this interaction requires the juxtamembrane and C-terminal tyrosines of Flt-2.
VEGF receptor tyrosine kinase autophosphorylation is a critical component in the regulation of PLC gamma binding and activation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VEGF binds to both Flt- 1 and KDR receptors, which are tyrosine kinse receptors.
the juxtamembrane and carboxy-terminal domains of the VEGF receptors are important for the interaction with PLC gamma and that the juxtemembrane domain is the most important for the interaction.
VEGF binding to Flt-1 or KDR induces the phosphorylation of tyrosine residues in the juxtamembrane and C-terminal regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the juxtamembrane and C-terminal regions are the major sites of interaction with PLC gamma and that the +1,2,3 amino acids following these tyrosine residues are important for binding.
the N-SH domain of PLC gamma has a higher affinity for the juxta membrane tyrosines, while the C-SH domain has a higher affinity to the C-tail tyrosines.
PLC gamma is a potential substrate for both Flt- and KDR-mediated signaling.
